text.p: The first official visit by a Jamaican prime minister to Haiti ended on Sunday with the signing of a friendship pact that included extending $3 million in trade credits to the hemisphere's poorest nation.

The two countries agreed to increase trade relations, work together to combat the growing threat of drug trafficking in the Caribbean, reopen air traffic and improve contacts between the private business communities of Haiti and Jamaica.

"I speak for all CARICOM members when I say we are anxious to embrace Haiti into the fold of the Caribbean family, fully and as soon as possible," Jamaican Prime Minister P.J. Patterson, the incoming president of the Caribbean Community, said at a news conference.
Relations between the two nations were cool during the 30-year reign of Haiti's Duvalier family, and this visit marked the reopening of relations, officials said.

"We wish to work together in preparations for free trade in the year 2005. To compete in today's global environment we have to have a strong united front. That is one reason for our visit to Haiti," Patterson said.
Haitian President Rene Preval and other Caribbean leaders were scheduled to attend a CARICOM meeting in Antigua later this month.
"This visit is a concrete act that indicates Haiti's return to the world community, but more importantly to the Caribbean community," Preval said at the news conference.
